review.title: Wrong Eagle, Wrong Blair
review.headline: Two Farm players got eggsecuted on bad egg math while one lone cat won.
review.summary: Round 1 had one Meowfia, Casey, who hid with a Kookaburra claim while the table piled onto Farm Eagle Alex over a visitor-count quibble. Round 2 went the other way: Casey's Hawk claim contradicted Blair's clean Kookaburra report, and the table caught her. In round 3 Drew, a Sphinx, hid behind a confused Kookaburra's unexplained +3 while Ellis's correct Hawk read was ignored. Blair was eggsecuted and Drew banked the win. Alex and Blair tied at 12 with Drew third on 10.

rounds.recap: Only Casey was Meowfia. Alex's Eagle +1 was argued as if it should be +2 because Alex also visited Drew, though the app did not count it. Everyone threw at Alex, a Farm player, and Casey won with a fake Kookaburra claim.
Casey, a Floofer, claimed Hawk on Blair. Blair's Kookaburra had no confusion line, so Casey's visit claim looked false. Everyone threw at her and Farm won. Casey's hug on Finley did nothing.

Ellis's Hawk gained an egg, which proved Drew was Meowfia, and he said so. The table instead chased Blair, whose confused report showed +3. Ellis got only three throws at Drew, and Blair, a Farm player, was eggsecuted. Drew won as lone Meowfia.

highlights.text: Alex's correct Eagle count was called a lie, and five of six players threw at a Farm Eagle.
Casey's Hawk-on-Blair claim collided with Blair's clean Kookaburra report, and the whole table converged on her.
Ellis correctly named Drew from a Hawk egg and put three cards on him, but the others ignored him.
Blair, confused, honestly admitted she could not explain her +3, and the table threw her out anyway.

confusions.what: Argued that Alex's visit to Drew counted as a visitor and so Eagle should gain +2. The app evidently did not count Alex's own visit.
First said Alex's +1 was unexplained, ignoring that an Eagle gains from its target's visitors. Finley later switched to agreeing with Drew.
Told Drew that Drew had been visited, though Drew's report showed no visitors. Drew was not an Eagle target.
Said Alex's +1 came from Ellis's own visit as Falcon. Falcon visits do not lay eggs on the target, and Alex's egg came from Alex's Eagle.
Claimed Hawk visits confuse a Kookaburra. Only a visit to a Kookaburra confuses her, and the claim was hard to check from any report.
Said Casey visited Blair, so Blair might be confused. He treated Casey's claim as true while the table was testing it.
Said Finley's Turkey +0 contradicted Alex's visit. A Turkey lays eggs in visitors' nests, not their own.
Said Alex's Falcon +2 did not fit a Falcon visit. The Turkey egg explained it, as Finley then pointed out.
Pointed at Ellis's Hawk claim as not matching Blair's own confused Eagle result. Confusion makes such results meaningless.

worked: Confused (Kookaburra, round 3): it produced a real, honest dilemma, since Blair could not clear herself and said so.
Cross-checking egg counts against claims: Casey's Hawk lie in round 2 was caught this way.
Hawk's egg on a Meowfia target gave a hard fact and a clear, tense decision about whether to trust Ellis.
problems: Hawk's proof was ignored in round 3. Ellis gave a hard fact and the table still voted Blair. Consider making the vote hold more weight from a verified claim, or a Hawk result that others can check.
Eagle and visitor counting was ambiguous in round 1 (does the Eagle's own visit count?). The rules need to state whether the visitor counts the Eagle itself, or Farm will argue over it.
Round 1 had only one Meowfia and no real cover for the table to examine. Five players threw at a Farm player over a rules quibble, so a round can go wrong from rules debate alone.

Confusion and Turkey/Owl egg sources make egg-count logic muddy. A confused player gives numbers nobody can use, and it is easy to blame them. Showing the cause of an egg in the dawn report would help.
Most throws were Wilds or one low card, so the bank-or-keep decision barely mattered. Scores moved little, and a bigger reward for correct throws would sharpen risk.
